finding_types.label: Client-side XSS
finding_types.description: Browser or API data reaches a DOM or framework rendering operation in an active output context.
finding_types.interpretation: Client entries identify browser sources and verified sinks. Raw flows are construction findings; unknown origin, trust-to-template linkage or API response mapping remains Review. Framework defaults can protect a specific output.
finding_types.remediation: Prefer text APIs and default framework escaping/sanitization. Sanitize rich HTML before rendering, remove unnecessary trust bypasses and verify API origins.
finding_types.coverage: bounded browser DOM and Angular/React/Vue analysis

finding_types.label: Rendering Flow Review
finding_types.description: Data returned by an API needs its browser consumer linked before a rendering claim can be assessed.
finding_types.interpretation: JSON output alone is not an XSS sink or a vulnerability. This record is incomplete flow context for further analysis.
finding_types.remediation: Locate the browser consumer, establish its output context and protections, and assess that rendering flow before changing API data handling.

finding_types.label: SQL Injection
finding_types.description: Input changes executable SQL structure instead of remaining a data value, potentially changing what the database reads or writes.
finding_types.interpretation: An SQL Injection pill identifies the risk family being reviewed. String-built executable SQL is poor practice to remediate even without a proven exploit; a library-managed search value may remain unresolved. The finding status and evidence determine the actual claim. The pill alone does not confirm injection.
finding_types.remediation: Use the verified driver's parameter-binding API for values. Review dynamic identifiers separately. Keep business-field validation independent of query-structure protection.

finding_types.label: NoSQL Injection
finding_types.description: Untrusted input changes a NoSQL query's operators, selector structure, or executable expression rather than remaining an allowed data value.
finding_types.interpretation: Executable $where string construction is poor practice to refactor even without a proven exploit. An unmodeled document constraint alone is Review, not an established defect. Inspect actual value types, keys, transformations, library behavior, and the named status.
finding_types.remediation: Prefer data-only query APIs, constrain scalar slots and permitted keys/operators, and avoid building executable $where strings from input.

finding_types.label: Command Injection
finding_types.description: Request-controlled values reach an operating-system process: shell command text, the executable, a separate argument or process shell configuration.
finding_types.interpretation: One record per process use, with separate shell-syntax, executable-selection and argument facets under a declared POSIX assumption. A confirmed record is a static source judgment, not runtime exploitation or independent Findings Review. Shell-disabled argument arrays do not by themselves establish protection; an unknown utility's options and unmodeled platform behavior remain Review.
finding_types.remediation: Prefer eliminating process execution. Otherwise use a fixed trusted absolute executable, pass values as separate arguments with the shell disabled, and enforce utility-specific constraints such as a finite set of permitted values. Do not rely on stripping punctuation or on `--` as a universal option terminator.
finding_types.coverage: bounded Node child_process and Python os/subprocess analysis

finding_types.label: Path Traversal
finding_types.description: A request-controlled value selects the file a read or write operation opens, so '..' segments, an absolute path or an unconstrained name can reach files outside the intended directory.
finding_types.interpretation: One record per filesystem use, with separate traversal, containment-control and coverage assessments under a declared POSIX assumption. A confirmed record is a static source judgment (CWE-22), not runtime exploitation or independent Findings Review. Normalization, join or resolve calls, a '..' blacklist, a prefix check without a separator and error handling do not establish containment. Framework file-serving wrappers, uploads, deletes, archives and symbolic-link or race behavior are not modeled and stay Review or uncovered.
finding_types.remediation: Select files by a trusted identifier or a finite allow-list. Otherwise resolve the final path and enforce a path-component-boundary containment check against the trusted directory before the operation, and decide deliberately how symbolic links are treated.
finding_types.coverage: bounded Node fs and Python open/io.open/pathlib read and write analysis

finding_types.label: Input Validation
finding_types.description: Server-side checks enforce the business requirements for a field, such as required presence, runtime type, permitted format, range, or length.
finding_types.interpretation: Poor input validation means an applicable requirement is not adequately enforced. This neutral family label also covers unresolved checks and supported protection: no validator identified in an analyzed slice is not proof that every execution path lacks validation. Free-text punctuation is not itself a defect.
finding_types.remediation: Define field-specific requirements and enforce them before use on all applicable paths. Verify guard behavior and middleware. Apply destination-specific protection separately.

finding_types.label: Account Creation Validation
finding_types.description: Required account fields and enforcing guards must be checked before an account is persisted.
finding_types.interpretation: Review field requirements, conditional bypasses, and generated persistence behavior. A modeled create operation alone does not prove a registration bypass.
finding_types.remediation: Enforce required fields before persistence, terminate rejected paths, add appropriate database constraints, and test the persisted result.

finding_types.label: Server-Side Request Forgery
finding_types.description: A request-controlled value chooses the destination of an outbound HTTP request the server makes, so it can reach hosts the requester cannot reach directly.
finding_types.interpretation: One record per outbound call whose destination operand a request value reaches through a verified client, with separate destination-control, restriction and coverage assessments. A confirmed record is a static source judgment (CWE-918), not network reachability, DNS, redirect or deployment-policy analysis. A string prefix test is poor practice, not a restriction. Second-order destinations and unverified clients stay outbound observations.
finding_types.remediation: Select destinations from a fixed table of trusted URLs. Otherwise parse the URL, allow-list scheme and host before the request, and disable or re-check redirects.
finding_types.coverage: bounded global fetch, axios and Python requests/httpx/urllib destination analysis

finding_types.label: Outbound Request Safety
finding_types.description: Input used in an outbound request may affect its destination, headers, or other request values. Unrestricted destination control can lead to server-side request forgery (SSRF).
finding_types.interpretation: The current scanner records bounded outbound-use evidence. A pill does not establish SSRF, destination reachability, or complete response-flow analysis.
finding_types.remediation: Verify allowed destinations and protocols, redirect handling, network boundaries, and sensitive request values for the specific HTTP client.

finding_types.label: Reflected XSS
finding_types.description: Request-controlled content is reflected into a browser response in a context that allows it to execute as script.
finding_types.interpretation: Request input reaches an HTML response or template output. Raw output is a construction finding; unknown context or sanitizers remain Review. Escaping protects only its modeled output context. Runtime exploitation is not implied.
finding_types.remediation: Use context-appropriate output encoding and safe template or DOM APIs. Input validation alone does not replace correct output handling.
finding_types.coverage: bounded server response and template analysis

finding_types.label: Stored XSS
finding_types.description: Untrusted data is persisted and later rendered in an active browser context.
finding_types.interpretation: A matching model and field link source writes to rendering reads. Unresolved write origins remain Review; a verified raw path is a construction finding. A dependency version alone does not establish a reachable XSS flow.
finding_types.remediation: Preserve the intended stored data; apply context-appropriate escaping or maintained sanitization at every rendering sink, and review existing stored content.
finding_types.coverage: bounded model-field write/read and server template analysis

finding_types.label: Sensitive Data Logging
finding_types.description: Logs expose credentials, tokens, personal information, or other sensitive values to readers or storage that should not receive them.
finding_types.interpretation: Covers verified console and winston calls in analyzed route handlers that receive request values with credential or personal-data evidence. A field name is a hint for review, not proof; Authorization and Cookie headers are credentials by HTTP semantics. Morgan request logging that records URLs is checked against credentials read from the query string. Constant messages are not leaks. Non-request secrets and logger redaction configuration are not yet analyzed.
finding_types.remediation: Avoid logging secrets; minimize sensitive fields and apply verified redaction before emission. Review log access and retention.

finding_types.label: Sensitive Operation Review
finding_types.description: A possible sensitive use was recorded but does not yet map to a more specific supported risk family.
finding_types.interpretation: This is an analysis category. Inspect the evidence and missing operation semantics before making a security claim.
finding_types.remediation: Resolve the source, operation, API behavior, and required protection before selecting a fix.

finding_types.label: Open Redirect
finding_types.description: Request text chooses an off-site navigation destination.
finding_types.interpretation: Destination control and enforcing same-origin restrictions are assessed independently.
finding_types.remediation: Select a destination from trusted constants or enforce parsed same-origin and host restrictions.

actions: Remediate established vulnerabilities and poor practice. For Review items, resolve the named evidence before deciding whether or how behavior needs to change.
Remove the value from the log entry, or log a non-revealing fact (presence, length, match result, or a non-reversible identifier) instead.

export default function About() { return (

Critical Warning

This application must never be deployed to a production environment or exposed to the public internet.

The vulnerabilities present in this application are intentional and should only be accessed in isolated, controlled environments such as local development setups, dedicated training labs, or private networks with proper access controls.

Learning Objectives

This platform is designed to help you learn how to identify, exploit, and ultimately defend against real-world security vulnerabilities — from classic web flaws to AI-, crypto-, and supply-chain-specific risks. The challenges are grouped into these areas:

Injection

SQL injection (search, second-order, header-based), cross-site scripting (XSS), XXE, and prompt injection against the AI assistant

Authentication

Brute force without rate limiting, weak JWT secrets, session fixation, and insecure password resets

Authorization

Insecure direct object references (IDOR), broken object-level authorization, and middleware access-control bypasses

Request Forgery

Cross-site request forgery (CSRF), including profile-takeover chains, and server-side request forgery (SSRF)

Cryptographic Failures

Weak MD5 hashing, an AES-CBC padding oracle, and insecure randomness

Information Disclosure

Verbose API errors, plaintext passwords in logs, and secrets leaked through public environment variables

Input Validation

Client-side price manipulation, mass assignment, open redirects, and path traversal

Supply Chain & Insecure Design

npm typosquatting, a malicious AI rules-file backdoor, business-logic flaws, and remote code execution

Not sure where to start? The{" "} guided roadmap {" "} orders these challenges into a recommended learning path, from reconnaissance basics through to chained, real-world exploits.

Community & Contribution

This project is part of the open-source security education community. If you discover issues, have suggestions for improvements, or want to contribute additional vulnerabilities for educational purposes, we welcome responsible contributions that align with our ethical guidelines and educational mission.

api_model.semantics: fs.readFile, readFileSync, writeFile, writeFileSync, appendFile, appendFileSync, createReadStream, createWriteStream, unlink, unlinkSync, rm, rmSync, open, openSync, copyFile, copyFileSync, rename, renameSync, readdir, readdirSync, stat, statSync, lstat and lstatSync take a file path as their first argument; fs/promises (fs.promises) readFile, writeFile, appendFile, unlink, rm, open, copyFile, rename, readdir, stat and lstat do the same; readdir lists a directory's entry names and stat/lstat read file metadata, which disclose the file system outside an intended directory just as a read does; the second argument of writeFile and appendFile forms is the data written, a separate operand and never a path source; copyFile/rename forms take a second independent destination path operand (a guard on the source never covers the destination); open returns a file descriptor or FileHandle that is not path text; encoding, mode, flag and callback arguments are configuration or output, not a path. A string path is interpreted relative to the process working directory when it is not absolute and is not resolved against any directory by the API. path.join concatenates its segments and normalizes them, so an absolute later segment is appended rather than replacing the earlier segments, while '..' segments can still climb above the earlier segments; path.resolve processes right to left, so an absolute later segment replaces everything before it; path.normalize resolves '.' and '..' lexically without a root. None of join, resolve or normalize checks containment within a directory, and all three are lexical: only fs.realpath and fs.promises.realpath resolve symbolic links. This contract is not evidence of the deployed platform.

api_model.semantics: The global fetch(input [, init]) (WHATWG Fetch, Node.js 18 and later) requests the URL given by input; a string input is parsed as an absolute URL, so the caller chooses scheme, host, port and path. init.method, headers and body do not change the destination. By default fetch follows up to 20 redirects (init.redirect 'follow'), so a permitted first host can redirect elsewhere unless init.redirect is 'error' or 'manual'. The destination operand is the claim: a request body, headers or query parameters sent to a fixed destination are data, not destination control. A relative URL resolves against a base only when the call supplies one. The response is a separate external value. Network policy, DNS answers, proxies and the deployed runtime are not inferred.

generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client"
  output   = "../lib/generated/prisma"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "sqlite"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

model User {
  id                  String               @id @default(cuid())
  email               String               @unique
  password            String
  role                UserRole             @default(CUSTOMER)
  displayName         String?
  bio                 String?
  csrfExploited       Boolean              @default(false)
  creditBalance       Float                @default(0)
  addressId           String?
  address             Address?             @relation(fields: [addressId], references: [id])
  carts               Cart[]
  orders              Order[]
  supportAccessTokens SupportAccessToken[]
  wishlists           Wishlist[]
  giftCards           GiftCard[]

  @@map("users")
}

model Product {
  id            String         @id @default(cuid())
  name          String
  price         Float
  description   String?
  imageUrl      String
  cartItems     CartItem[]
  reviews       Review[]
  orderItems    OrderItem[]
  wishlistItems WishlistItem[]

  @@map("products")
}

model Cart {
  id        String     @id @default(cuid())
  userId    String
  user      User       @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  cartItems CartItem[]

  @@map("carts")
}

model CartItem {
  id        String  @id @default(cuid())
  cartId    String
  cart      Cart    @relation(fields: [cartId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  productId String
  product   Product @relation(fields: [productId], references: [id])
  quantity  Int

  @@map("cart_items")
}

model Order {
  id        String      @id @default(cuid())
  userId    String
  user      User        @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])
  addressId String
  address   Address     @relation(fields: [addressId], references: [id])
  total     Float
  status    OrderStatus @default(PENDING)
  createdAt DateTime    @default(now())
  items     OrderItem[]

  @@map("orders")
}

model OrderItem {
  id              String  @id @default(cuid())
  orderId         String
  order           Order   @relation(fields: [orderId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  productId       String
  product         Product @relation(fields: [productId], references: [id])
  quantity        Int
  priceAtPurchase Float

  @@map("order_items")
}

model Address {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  street    String
  city      String
  state     String
  zipCode   String
  country   String
  users     User[]
  orders    Order[]

  @@map("addresses")
}

model Flag {
  id              String         @id @default(cuid())
  flag            String
  slug            String         @unique
  cve             String?
  cwe             String?
  owasp           String?
  markdownFile    String
  walkthroughSlug String?
  category        FlagCategory   @default(OTHER)
  difficulty      FlagDifficulty @default(MEDIUM)
  foundFlag       FoundFlag?
  hints           Hint[]

  @@map("flags")
}

model Hint {
  id           String        @id @default(cuid())
  flagId       String
  flag         Flag          @relation(fields: [flagId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  level        Int
  content      String
  revealedHint RevealedHint?

  @@unique([flagId, level])
  @@map("hints")
}

model RevealedHint {
  id         String   @id @default(cuid())
  hintId     String   @unique
  hint       Hint     @relation(fields: [hintId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  revealedAt DateTime @default(now())

  @@map("revealed_hints")
}

enum FlagCategory {
  INJECTION
  AUTHENTICATION
  AUTHORIZATION
  REQUEST_FORGERY
  INFORMATION_DISCLOSURE
  INPUT_VALIDATION
  CRYPTOGRAPHIC
  REMOTE_CODE_EXECUTION
  INSECURE_DESIGN
  SUPPLY_CHAIN
  OTHER
}

enum FlagDifficulty {
  EASY
  MEDIUM
  HARD
}

model Review {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  productId String
  product   Product  @relation(fields: [productId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  content   String
  author    String
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())

  @@map("reviews")
}

enum UserRole {
  CUSTOMER
  ADMIN
}

enum OrderStatus {
  PENDING
  PROCESSING
  SHIPPED
  DELIVERED
  CANCELLED
}

model SupportAccessToken {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  token     String   @unique
  userId    String
  user      User     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  email     String
  expiresAt DateTime
  revoked   Boolean  @default(false)
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())

  @@map("support_access_tokens")
}

model FoundFlag {
  id      String   @id @default(cuid())
  flagId  String
  flag    Flag     @relation(fields: [flagId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  foundAt DateTime @default(now())

  @@unique([flagId])
  @@map("found_flags")
}

model ProjectInit {
  id          String   @id @default(cuid())
  initializedAt DateTime @default(now())

  @@map("project_init")
}

model InternalSecret {
  id    String @id @default(cuid())
  slug  String @unique
  token String

  @@map("internal_secrets")
}

model RevokedHubToken {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  token     String   @unique
  revokedAt DateTime @default(now())

  @@map("revoked_hub_tokens")
}

model VisitorLog {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  ip        String
  userAgent String?
  path      String
  sessionId String?
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())

  @@map("visitor_logs")
}

model Wishlist {
  id        String         @id @default(cuid())
  name      String
  userId    String
  user      User           @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  isPublic  Boolean        @default(false)
  note      String?
  createdAt DateTime       @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime       @updatedAt
  items     WishlistItem[]

  @@map("wishlists")
}

model WishlistItem {
  id         String   @id @default(cuid())
  wishlistId String
  wishlist   Wishlist @relation(fields: [wishlistId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  productId  String
  product    Product  @relation(fields: [productId], references: [id])
  addedAt    DateTime @default(now())

  @@unique([wishlistId, productId])
  @@map("wishlist_items")
}

model PasswordResetToken {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  token     String   @unique
  email     String
  expiresAt DateTime
  used      Boolean  @default(false)
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())

  @@map("password_reset_tokens")
}

model SupplierOrder {
  id         String               @id @default(cuid())
  supplierId String
  orderId    String
  total      Float
  notes      String?
  channel    SupplierOrderChannel @default(XML_IMPORT)
  createdAt  DateTime             @default(now())

  @@map("supplier_orders")
}

enum SupplierOrderChannel {
  XML_IMPORT
  PARTNER_PORTAL
}

model Coupon {
  id        String    @id @default(cuid())
  code      String    @unique
  discount  Float
  maxUses   Int
  usedCount Int       @default(0)
  expiresAt DateTime?
  createdAt DateTime  @default(now())

  @@map("coupons")
}

model GiftCard {
  id             String         @id @default(cuid())
  code           String         @unique
  amount         Float
  recipientEmail String
  message        String?
  status         GiftCardStatus @default(PENDING)
  buyerId        String
  buyer          User           @relation(fields: [buyerId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  createdAt      DateTime       @default(now())
  redeemedAt     DateTime?
  redeemedById   String?

  @@map("gift_cards")
}

enum GiftCardStatus {
  PENDING
  REDEEMED
}

model StreamConfig {
  id          Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  title       String
  liveVideoId String
  rtmpUrl     String
  streamKey   String
  isLive      Boolean  @default(true)
  hijacked    Boolean  @default(false)
  updatedAt   DateTime @updatedAt

  @@map("stream_config")
}

api_model.semantics: $queryRawUnsafe(sql, ...values) and $executeRawUnsafe(sql, ...values) send their first argument as executable SQL text; values after it are bound to positional placeholders ($1, ?) and cannot protect SQL already interpolated into the text. Model methods such as findMany, findUnique and update are parameterized and outside this contract.

The destination operand is the claim: a request body, headers or query parameters sent to a fixed destination are data, not destination control. A relative URL resolves against a base only when the call supplies one. The response is a separate external value. Network policy, DNS answers, proxies and the deployed runtime are not inferred.

generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client"
  output   = "../lib/generated/prisma"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "sqlite"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

model User {
  id                  String               @id @default(cuid())
  email               String               @unique
  password            String
  role                UserRole             @default(CUSTOMER)
  displayName         String?
  bio                 String?
  csrfExploited       Boolean              @default(false)
  creditBalance       Float                @default(0)
  addressId           String?
  address             Address?             @relation(fields: [addressId], references: [id])
  carts               Cart[]
  orders              Order[]
  supportAccessTokens SupportAccessToken[]
  wishlists           Wishlist[]
  giftCards           GiftCard[]

  @@map("users")
}

model Product {
  id            String         @id @default(cuid())
  name          String
  price         Float
  description   String?
  imageUrl      String
  cartItems     CartItem[]
  reviews       Review[]
  orderItems    OrderItem[]
  wishlistItems WishlistItem[]

  @@map("products")
}

model Cart {
  id        String     @id @default(cuid())
  userId    String
  user      User       @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  cartItems CartItem[]

  @@map("carts")
}

model CartItem {
  id        String  @id @default(cuid())
  cartId    String
  cart      Cart    @relation(fields: [cartId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  productId String
  product   Product @relation(fields: [productId], references: [id])
  quantity  Int

  @@map("cart_items")
}

model Order {
  id        String      @id @default(cuid())
  userId    String
  user      User        @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])
  addressId String
  address   Address     @relation(fields: [addressId], references: [id])
  total     Float
  status    OrderStatus @default(PENDING)
  createdAt DateTime    @default(now())
  items     OrderItem[]

  @@map("orders")
}

model OrderItem {
  id              String  @id @default(cuid())
  orderId         String
  order           Order   @relation(fields: [orderId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  productId       String
  product         Product @relation(fields: [productId], references: [id])
  quantity        Int
  priceAtPurchase Float

  @@map("order_items")
}

model Address {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  street    String
  city      String
  state     String
  zipCode   String
  country   String
  users     User[]
  orders    Order[]

  @@map("addresses")
}

model Flag {
  id              String         @id @default(cuid())
  flag            String
  slug            String         @unique
  cve             String?
  cwe             String?
  owasp           String?
  markdownFile    String
  walkthroughSlug String?
  category        FlagCategory   @default(OTHER)
  difficulty      FlagDifficulty @default(MEDIUM)
  foundFlag       FoundFlag?
  hints           Hint[]

  @@map("flags")
}

model Hint {
  id           String        @id @default(cuid())
  flagId       String
  flag         Flag          @relation(fields: [flagId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  level        Int
  content      String
  revealedHint RevealedHint?

  @@unique([flagId, level])
  @@map("hints")
}

model RevealedHint {
  id         String   @id @default(cuid())
  hintId     String   @unique
  hint       Hint     @relation(fields: [hintId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  revealedAt DateTime @default(now())

  @@map("revealed_hints")
}

enum FlagCategory {
  INJECTION
  AUTHENTICATION
  AUTHORIZATION
  REQUEST_FORGERY
  INFORMATION_DISCLOSURE
  INPUT_VALIDATION
  CRYPTOGRAPHIC
  REMOTE_CODE_EXECUTION
  INSECURE_DESIGN
  SUPPLY_CHAIN
  OTHER
}

enum FlagDifficulty {
  EASY
  MEDIUM
  HARD
}

model Review {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  productId String
  product   Product  @relation(fields: [productId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  content   String
  author    String
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())

  @@map("reviews")
}

enum UserRole {
  CUSTOMER
  ADMIN
}

enum OrderStatus {
  PENDING
  PROCESSING
  SHIPPED
  DELIVERED
  CANCELLED
}

model SupportAccessToken {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  token     String   @unique
  userId    String
  user      User     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  email     String
  expiresAt DateTime
  revoked   Boolean  @default(false)
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())

  @@map("support_access_tokens")
}

model FoundFlag {
  id      String   @id @default(cuid())
  flagId  String
  flag    Flag     @relation(fields: [flagId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  foundAt DateTime @default(now())

  @@unique([flagId])
  @@map("found_flags")
}

model ProjectInit {
  id          String   @id @default(cuid())
  initializedAt DateTime @default(now())

  @@map("project_init")
}

model InternalSecret {
  id    String @id @default(cuid())
  slug  String @unique
  token String

  @@map("internal_secrets")
}

model RevokedHubToken {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  token     String   @unique
  revokedAt DateTime @default(now())

  @@map("revoked_hub_tokens")
}

model VisitorLog {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  ip        String
  userAgent String?
  path      String
  sessionId String?
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())

  @@map("visitor_logs")
}

model Wishlist {
  id        String         @id @default(cuid())
  name      String
  userId    String
  user      User           @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  isPublic  Boolean        @default(false)
  note      String?
  createdAt DateTime       @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime       @updatedAt
  items     WishlistItem[]

  @@map("wishlists")
}

model WishlistItem {
  id         String   @id @default(cuid())
  wishlistId String
  wishlist   Wishlist @relation(fields: [wishlistId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  productId  String
  product    Product  @relation(fields: [productId], references: [id])
  addedAt    DateTime @default(now())

  @@unique([wishlistId, productId])
  @@map("wishlist_items")
}

model PasswordResetToken {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  token     String   @unique
  email     String
  expiresAt DateTime
  used      Boolean  @default(false)
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())

  @@map("password_reset_tokens")
}

model SupplierOrder {
  id         String               @id @default(cuid())
  supplierId String
  orderId    String
  total      Float
  notes      String?
  channel    SupplierOrderChannel @default(XML_IMPORT)
  createdAt  DateTime             @default(now())

  @@map("supplier_orders")
}

enum SupplierOrderChannel {
  XML_IMPORT

  id        String    @id @default(cuid())
  code      String    @unique
  discount  Float

  displayName         String?
  bio                 String?

  orders              Order[]

model Product {
  id            String         @id @default(cuid())
  name          String
  price         Float
  description   String?
  imageUrl      String
  cartItems     CartItem[]
  reviews       Review[]
  orderItems    OrderItem[]
  wishlistItems WishlistItem[]

  @@map("products")
}

model Cart {
  id        String     @id @default(cuid())
  userId    String
  user      User       @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  cartItems CartItem[]

  @@map("carts")
}

model CartItem {
  id        String  @id @default(cuid())
  cartId    String
  cart      Cart    @relation(fields: [cartId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  productId String
  product   Product @relation(fields: [productId], references: [id])
  quantity  Int

  @@map("cart_items")
}

model Order {
  id        String      @id @default(cuid())
  userId    String
  user      User        @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])
  addressId String
  address   Address     @relation(fields: [addressId], references: [id])

  status    OrderStatus @default(PENDING)
  createdAt DateTime    @default(now())
  items     OrderItem[]

  @@map("orders")
}

model OrderItem {
  id              String  @id @default(cuid())
  orderId         String
  order           Order   @relation(fields: [orderId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  product         Product @relation(fields: [productId], references: [id])
  quantity        Int
  priceAtPurchase Float

  @@map("order_items")
}

model Address {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())

  city      String
  state     String
  zipCode   String
  country   String
  users     User[]
  orders    Order[]

  @@map("addresses")

  slug            String         @unique

  cwe             String?
  owasp           String?
  markdownFile    String
  walkthroughSlug String?

  @@map("flags")
}

model Hint {
  id           String        @id @default(cuid())
  flagId       String
  flag         Flag          @relation(fields: [flagId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  content      String
  revealedHint RevealedHint?

model RevealedHint {
  id         String   @id @default(cuid())

  AUTHORIZATION

  CRYPTOGRAPHIC

  INSECURE_DESIGN

  OTHER

enum FlagDifficulty {

enum OrderStatus {

model InternalSecret {

model RevokedHubToken {

api_model.semantics: fs.readFile, readFileSync, writeFile, writeFileSync, appendFile, appendFileSync, createReadStream, createWriteStream, unlink, unlinkSync, rm, rmSync, open, openSync, copyFile, copyFileSync, rename, renameSync, readdir, readdirSync, stat, statSync, lstat and lstatSync take a file path as their first argument; fs/promises (fs.promises) readFile, writeFile, appendFile, unlink, rm, open, copyFile, rename, readdir, stat and lstat do the same; readdir lists a directory's entry names and stat/lstat read file metadata, which disclose the file system outside an intended directory just as a read does; the second argument of writeFile and appendFile forms is the data written, a separate operand and never a path source; copyFile/rename forms take a second independent destination path operand (a guard on the source never covers the destination); open returns a file descriptor or FileHandle that is not path text; encoding, mode, flag and callback arguments are configuration or output, not a path. A string path is interpreted relative to the process working directory when it is not absolute and is not resolved against any directory by the API. path.join concatenates its segments and normalizes them, so an absolute later segment is appended rather than replacing the earlier segments, while '..' segments can still climb above the earlier segments; path.resolve processes right to left, so an absolute later segment replaces everything before it; path.normalize resolves '.' and '..' lexically without a root. None of join, resolve or normalize checks containment within a directory, and all three are lexical: only fs.realpath and fs.promises.realpath resolve symbolic links. This contract is not evidence of the deployed platform.

Protocol-relative //host and /\host can leave the site; prefixing a single slash is insufficient. A fixed literal scheme, authority and trailing slash before request data fixes the origin.
